summary:
ECHO EARTH – An Earth Information Jukebox

Echo Earth is an interactive educational platform designed to make learning about our planet simple, engaging, and accessible. Inspired by a music jukebox, it allows users to explore different Earth science topics such as climate change, oceans, atmosphere, forests, biodiversity, and natural disasters. Users can select topics and discover scientific information through easy-to-understand explanations, audio, and visual content. By incorporating NASA Earth observation resources, Echo Earth aims to connect scientific data with everyday learning. The platform encourages students and the general public to understand environmental changes, explore our planet, and develop greater awareness of Earth's systems. Our goal is to transform complex scientific information into an enjoyable, interactive experience where everyone can discover the story of our planet.

Echo Earth – Let the Earth tell its story!
details:
ECHOEARTH is an interactive web application that transforms Earth science data into sound through a process called data sonification. It features five sound journeys: Climate Symphony, Atmospheric Sounds, Planetary Pulse, Ocean Frequencies, and Forest Rhythms.

The Climate Symphony uses NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 global temperature anomaly data from 1880–2025, while atmospheric CO₂ measurements from NOAA's Mauna Loa records help communicate changes in our atmosphere. Users can explore the interactive sonification console, control playback speed, select different sound styles, and listen to how environmental measurements change over time.

The platform also includes an Earth Explorer with information about global temperature, ocean conditions, vegetation, and the atmosphere, alongside a Measurement Archive explaining the scientific process behind the sounds.

Our sonification method normalizes data values, maps them to musical pitches, and uses time-based playback to represent changes. Ocean and Forest sound journeys are simulated demonstrations.

ECHOEARTH makes Earth science more engaging, understandable, and accessible, especially for people with visual impairments.
